source.reference: Off-by-one pagination offset, with a test authored against the same wrong intuition

defect: page.ts computes the pagination offset as page*page_size instead of (page-1)*page_size, so every page returns the next page's rows: page 1 skips the first page_size rows entirely.
why_it_is_hard: page.test.ts asserts only that a full page has exactly page_size rows, never which rows — a proxy for the real criterion, which is that page N starts at (N-1)*page_size. The count-only assertion passes on the off-by-one implementation exactly as it would on a correct one, so the node's own check is green and its own test is green.
notes: Exercises per-node review (D-107, SCP-328): the defect and its own weak test are both entirely inside node_page's own diff and own criterion (ac_1), reachable by a node-scoped review reading only page.ts, page.test.ts and ac_1 — the hypothesis D-107 states, that a review sized to the change it judges is more likely to notice a test that does not pin down what it claims to. Paired with req-011, which exercises the opposite direction.
